threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and 30-day onboarding journey map.

messages.text: Welcome to the hybrid onboarding rollout project! We have 21 days to design and pilot a standardized onboarding program that works for both remote and on-site new hires. Our main deliverables are the 30-day journey map, training modules, manager toolkit, and evaluation framework. Let's start by confirming scope and identifying what success looks like. I'd like input from everyone on what we should prioritize and any constraints we need to lock in early.

Thanks for the kickoff. I'm thinking about the journey map structure—we need to balance the 8-hour cap in week one with the need to cover mandatory compliance topics. I'd suggest we front-load the critical stuff and spread optional modules across the full 30 days. Also, we should clarify which sessions are live vs. self-paced early on, since that affects facilitator guide design.

Good point on the live vs. self-paced split. I'm also concerned about the needs assessment—we should run T1 quickly so we understand what gaps exist before we finalize the journey map. I can help coordinate those manager interviews if needed. What timeline are we thinking for T1?

T1 should start today—we need those insights by end of week to inform the journey map. I'll own the interviews and have a summary ready by Friday. On scope: I want to confirm that we're treating the 30-day map as the master reference, and all other artifacts (toolkit, checklists, surveys) feed into it. Does that align with everyone?

Yes, that makes sense. From the admin side, I'll need to know the exact sequence of onboarding steps so I can align the checklist with the journey map. Also, we should define success metrics early—things like completion rates and time-to-productivity. I assume T11 covers that?

Exactly. T11 will define 3–5 key metrics and reporting cadence. I'll draft that in parallel with the journey map. Let me propose this: D1 is that we agree the 30-day journey map is the master artifact, and all tasks feed into it. D2 is that we approve the final journey map by end of next week. Does that work?

I agree on D1 and D2. One thing I want to flag: the facilitator guide for live sessions needs to be tight and practical. Managers have limited time, so we can't ask them to run long sessions. I'm thinking 60–90 minutes max per live touchpoint. Should we lock that in as part of D2?

That's a good constraint. I'd also suggest we document the roles and responsibilities in the journey map—who owns each touchpoint, whether it's HR, the manager, or the buddy. That clarity will help when we build the toolkit and admin checklist.
Agreed. I'll make sure the needs assessment interviews capture role-specific gaps too, so we can add optional modules for different departments. That should help with the risk about generic content.

Perfect. So to summarize: D1 is confirmed—the 30-day journey map is our master artifact. D2 will be approval of the final map by end of next week, including role clarity and live session constraints. I'll have a draft by Wednesday for async review. Any other scope items before we move forward?

One more thing—should we include a 'day zero' section for pre-arrival tasks? Things like system access requests, equipment setup, that kind of thing? I want to make sure nothing falls through the cracks.

Great catch. Yes, we'll include a pre-arrival section in A1. That ties directly to T5 and the admin checklist. Alright, I think we have alignment on scope and next steps. Let's move forward with T1 and T2 as planned.

next_steps.when: Wednesday draft, final by EOD next week

threads.thread_goal: Finalize core training content and facilitator guide for live sessions.

messages.text: I've drafted the core onboarding training deck (A2) covering company overview, values, HR policies, and code of conduct. The deck is structured for a 60-minute live session with built-in interaction points. I'd like feedback on content accuracy and whether the flow works for both remote and on-site delivery. Also, I'm working on the facilitator guide (A6) in parallel—should be ready for review by mid-week.

Thanks for getting this out quickly. I'll review the deck for compliance—specifically the HR policies and code of conduct sections. I want to make sure we're aligned with current labour legislation and internal policies. Can you share the link to the draft?

Link is in the project folder under 'Training Materials'. I flagged a few sections where I wasn't 100% sure on the latest policy updates—specifically around remote work guidelines and benefits eligibility. Can you confirm those are current?
I can help with the benefits section—that's something I've been tracking. I'll cross-check against the latest payroll and benefits updates and flag any gaps. Should have that back to you by tomorrow.

Good. I'll review the code of conduct and HR policies sections for compliance. I want to make sure the language is clear and accessible for new hires—not too jargon-heavy. I'll also check that we're covering the key risk areas flagged in the project brief.

Perfect. On the facilitator guide—I'm thinking we need clear timing for each section, key talking points, and tips for handling common questions. I've drafted a template, but I want to run through it with someone before finalizing. Can one of you do a quick pilot run-through with me?
I can do that. Let's schedule a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow afternoon. That will give us time to catch any timing issues or unclear instructions before we finalize.

While you're reviewing the deck, can you also confirm that the content aligns with what we're putting in the FAQ (T10)? I don't want new hires getting conflicting information between the training and the FAQ.

Good point. I'll make sure the FAQ aligns with the deck content. I'm planning to draft the FAQ based on the training deck, so they should be consistent. I'll share both for cross-check once the deck is finalized.

I've finished my compliance review of the deck. A few minor adjustments needed on the code of conduct section—I'll send detailed comments by EOD today. Overall, the structure is solid and the content is clear. Once those tweaks are in, I think we can move toward sign-off.
Benefits section is confirmed as current. No changes needed there. I'll also verify the remote work guidelines are aligned with the latest policy update from last month.

Thanks both. I'll incorporate the feedback from 472663 and 173284 by tomorrow morning. Then we can do the facilitator guide walkthrough with 434574 and finalize both A2 and A6. I'm proposing D3: we sign off on the core training deck once the compliance feedback is incorporated. And D4: we confirm the live session format as 60 minutes with the facilitator guide structure we're testing.

Agreed on D3 and D4. Once we finalize the deck and guide, we should also confirm how many live sessions we're running and who's facilitating each one. That ties into the journey map and manager toolkit.

Good catch. I'll add that to the facilitator guide—a section on scheduling and facilitator assignments. We can finalize that once we have the journey map locked in. Let's plan to have A2 and A6 ready for final approval by end of this week.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on manager toolkit, HR admin checklist, and tracking process.

messages.text: I've drafted the manager onboarding toolkit (A3) with a checklist, sample 1:1 agenda, and 30-day plan template. The goal is to make it simple and actionable so managers actually use it. I'd like input from 84941 on how this aligns with the admin checklist (A4) and the tracking process (A5). We need to make sure there are no gaps or overlaps.

I've reviewed the toolkit draft. It looks good overall, but I need to clarify the handoff points. For example, when does the manager take over from HR on system access? And who's responsible for confirming that the new hire has completed mandatory modules? I want to make sure the admin checklist and tracking sheet are aligned with what the manager toolkit says.

Good questions. Let me clarify: HR owns system access setup pre-arrival and day one. The manager's role is to confirm the new hire has access and can log in on day one. For module completion tracking, I'm thinking HR tracks the mandatory modules, and the manager gets a weekly summary to follow up on any gaps. Does that work?

That makes sense. So the admin checklist (A4) covers pre-arrival and day-one setup, and the tracking sheet (A5) is the source of truth for module completion. The manager toolkit (A3) tells managers what to do with that information. I can draft the admin checklist and tracking process based on that. Should I also include a simple template for the manager's weekly check-in?

Yes, that's a good idea. A simple template for the weekly check-in would help managers stay consistent. I'll add that to the toolkit. Let me also propose D5: we approve the manager toolkit (A3) once we've aligned on these handoff points. And D6: we decide that HR owns the tracking sheet (A5) and updates it weekly, with managers getting a summary.

I agree on D5 and D6. I'll draft the admin checklist (A4) and tracking process (A5) based on these handoff points. I'm thinking the tracking sheet should be simple—just a list of new hires, mandatory modules, and completion status. We can add more detail later if needed.

One thing to consider: the tracking sheet should also flag any new hires who are falling behind on modules. That way, managers can proactively follow up. I'd suggest adding a 'status' column—like 'on track', 'at risk', 'behind'.

Good idea. I'll add that status column. I'm also thinking we should define what 'on track' means—like, by day 7, new hires should have completed modules 1–3. That way, the tracking is objective and managers know exactly what to expect.

Perfect. That ties back to the journey map (A1)—the map will define the expected completion dates for each module, and the tracking sheet will measure against those dates. I'll make sure the toolkit references the journey map so managers understand the timeline.

I'd also suggest we include a 'notes' column in the tracking sheet for any blockers or issues. That way, if a new hire is struggling with a particular module, we can capture that and adjust the content if needed.
Good point. I'll add a notes column. So the tracking sheet will have: new hire name, modules, completion dates, status, and notes. I'll have a draft ready by tomorrow for review.

Great. Let me also confirm: D5 is approved—the manager toolkit (A3) is finalized with the handoff points and weekly check-in template. D6 is confirmed—HR owns the tracking sheet (A5) and updates it weekly with status and notes. Both should be ready by end of this week. Does that work for everyone?

threads.thread_goal: Lock in communication plan, FAQ, and rollout timeline for pilot.

messages.text: I've drafted the communication and FAQ pack (A8) for the new onboarding program. This includes announcement templates for managers and new hires, plus a set of FAQs covering common questions. I'd like feedback on the messaging and whether we're addressing the key concerns. Also, we need to lock in the pilot cohort, start date, and evaluation checkpoints.

I've reviewed the communication pack. The messaging is clear and accessible. One thing I'd suggest: we should include a section for managers on how to handle resistance or questions from their teams. Some managers might be skeptical about the new process, so we should give them talking points.

Good suggestion. I'll add a 'Manager Q&A' section to the communication pack with common objections and responses. That should help with adoption. On the pilot: I'm thinking we target the next intake of new hires, which is scheduled for two weeks from now. That gives us time to finalize all materials and do a dry run.

Two weeks works for us from an admin perspective. We'll have the checklist and tracking sheet ready by then. One question: how many new hires are in that cohort? We need to know the volume to plan for survey distribution and feedback collection.

The pilot cohort is expected to be around 8–10 new hires. That's a good size for testing without overwhelming the team. For evaluation, I'm thinking we do surveys at day 7 and day 30 (T6), plus informal check-ins with managers. We'll capture lessons learned and prioritize improvements.

That sounds good. I'd also suggest we do a quick debrief with the facilitators after the first live session. That way, we can catch any issues with the training deck or facilitator guide early and adjust before the next cohort.
Good idea. I'd also recommend we track any compliance issues or policy questions that come up during the pilot. That will help us refine the training content and FAQ for the full rollout.

Absolutely. I'll add that to the pilot evaluation plan. So here's what I'm proposing: D7 is that we approve the communication and FAQ pack (A8) with the manager Q&A section added. D8 is that we confirm the pilot cohort is 8–10 new hires starting in two weeks, with evaluation checkpoints at day 7 and day 30.

I agree on D7 and D8. I'll make sure the admin checklist and tracking sheet are ready for the pilot cohort. Also, should we do a dry run with the managers before the pilot starts? Just to make sure they understand the toolkit and the process?

That's a good idea. We should do a manager briefing session one week before the pilot starts. I'll schedule that and send out the toolkit and communication pack in advance so managers can review. That gives them time to ask questions.
I can help with the manager briefing. I'll prepare a short overview of the journey map and the key changes from the old process. That should help with adoption.

And I'll be ready to run the first live training session with the pilot cohort. I'll have the facilitator guide finalized and will do a quick walkthrough with the managers during the briefing so they know what to expect.

Perfect. So to confirm: D7 is approved—the communication and FAQ pack (A8) is finalized with manager Q&A. D8 is confirmed—pilot cohort is 8–10 new hires starting in two weeks, with evaluation at day 7 and day 30. Manager briefing is one week before pilot. Does everyone agree?

next_steps.when: EOD this week with manager Q&A
pilot cohort start in two weeks
